rule: Four open clauses of the campaign's success criteria were blocked on a ruling no implementation lane may write, and that fact was scattered across a report section, three escalation ledgers and a verify-ledger note. Scattered, it reads as four lanes each explaining why it stopped. Collected, it is one list with a length: these are the decisions the campaign owed itself, and nothing below closed by anybody trying harder. Every row names the criterion it blocked, the artifact carrying the measurement, the question in one sentence, and what a lane may NOT do instead -- because the second half is what keeps 'blocked on a ruling' from becoming the place work goes to stop. The first four were answered on 2026-08-14 by dated amendments in the umbrella; the rows moved to answered[] rather than being deleted, so the question, its measurement and its answer stay joined. A fifth was opened the same day, by the pass that closed the other four: a criterion cannot be discharged by the lane that discovers it is unmet. A sixth was opened by the pass that docketed the standing dissents, for the same reason and from the other end -- the one debt whose remedy is not an investigation, found by asking what a fresh investigator would be asked and finding no question; it was answered on 2026-08-15 by Amendment J, which adjudicates such a string by source assertion, and its row moved to answered[] rather than being deleted. A seventh was opened on the same day by the pass that sized the fourteen receipt-walk deferrals into slices: three of them name a retiring act the campaign's own criterion 8 forbids, which is a mis-description of a debt rather than a debt anybody can pay. The seventh was answered on 2026-08-15 by Amendment K, which rules the retiring act per LANE rather than per walk -- the interpreter in the family's own declared serving lane, which is the receipt walk for eleven of the rows and the defence resolver for the three whose via says so -- and its row moved to answered[] rather than being deleted. An eighth was opened on 2026-08-16 by the retirement lane that measured a family with no pair row to stamp, and answered the same day by Amendment O, which rules such a family PAIR_ONLY under the umbrella's own semantic-authority rule and closes its receipt-walk row as a schedule category error rather than a retirement -- with a machine check that reopens it, and with a one-pass triage of every remaining row so the sixth lane does not rediscover what stopped the fifth; its row moved to answered[] rather than being deleted. A ninth was opened on 2026-08-16 by the next retirement lane and from the opposite end of the same debt: three rows whose ruled retiring act is not missing but ALREADY PERFORMED, in a lane the deferral row is not keyed on, so no amount of doing the ruled act could ever move them. It was answered the same day by Amendment Q, which rules that a family whose walk-side need is served through its declared lane must not declare a receipt-walk lane at all, closes the three rows as lane-declaration corrections carrying a machine check in both directions and a reopening condition, and moved its row to answered[] rather than being deleted. A tenth was opened on 2026-08-16 by the retirement lane that reached the first family whose packet is DELIVERED AS A BASIC ATTACK SWING: the budgeted pricing stage carries a resistance and the holder's amps, and a swing meets three further target-side terms of which one -- a capped flat subtraction applied per crit outcome before the blend -- is not a factor any declared magnitude can carry, while the family's second authored row declares no magnitude at all and re-delivers another family's. It was answered the same day by Amendment R, which rules the swing composition onto the stage with the subtraction carried and never folded, widens the term census's predicate to authoring-time terms so the next such term is measured rather than tripped over, rules that a routing family declares no magnitude of its own, and orders a covering scenario that arms the enemy-held terms as an integration act; its row moved to answered[] rather than being deleted. That leaves one row open, and it is the first one: whether criterion 11's first clause binds the campaign backwards.
how_a_row_closes: The ruling is recorded in docs/plans/2026-08-08-silent-failure-campaign.md -- in the [H] table, in a decision row, or as a dated amendment, which is where Amendments A through D already live -- and the row moves to answered[] naming the amendment. A row does NOT close by a lane deciding the question is smaller than it looked, and it does not close by the criterion being re-read more weakly: umbrella criterion 11's own words are that a phase document may not write its own descope.
why_a_lane_may_not_write_these: Umbrella criterion 11: every [H] is either answered and recorded in the umbrella or its dependent slice is explicitly descoped there with its criterion restated -- a phase document may not write its own descope. The same reasoning reaches a success criterion an implementation would have to reinterpret to satisfy. Amendments A, B, C and D are the precedent: each was measured by a lane, refused by that lane, and recorded in the umbrella by its owner.

owed.blocks: runbook criterion 11's first clause -- every slice has a recorded verify-<slice> verdict
owed.measurement_artifact: docs/receipts/verify-ledger.json, coverage block, gated by tests/test_verify_ledger.py
owed.question: The clause has a machine denominator now and fails it backwards: 68 slice-group tags derived from commit subjects, one covered by a verdict recorded in this ledger, seven more citing a verdict in their own commit bodies with a sha a reader can open, and 61 citing nothing anywhere. R-35 was real and used -- the campaign answered NOT DISCHARGED verdicts by name -- but the verdicts were written into commit bodies rather than into an artifact, so most of them are unrecoverable as records. Does the clause bind the campaign's own past, in which case somebody schedules 61 fresh R-35 passes over closed ranges; or is it discharged forwards, by a ledger whose gate refuses the next slice group that ships without a verdict row or an explicit line?
owed.why_no_lane_may_answer_it: Both ways out are a lane deciding what a criterion means. Reading it forwards is a re-reading of 'every slice', which criterion 11's own words forbid a phase document from doing; reading it backwards commits somebody to sixty-one verification passes, which is a scheduling decision with a cost and an owner.
owed.what_a_lane_may_not_do_instead: Three things, and each has been available and refused. Manufacture a verdict for a slice nobody verified -- that is precisely the unverifiable claim about the past Phase 1 outlaws. Reconstruct verdicts from the commit bodies of the very lanes being checked, which is a record derived from the thing it is supposed to check independently. And shrink the denominator by declaring some tags 'not really slices', which is driving a counter to zero by editing what it counts.
owed.consequence_of_leaving_it_open: The clause holds forwards and is measured backwards. The gate refuses the next slice group that ships with neither a verdict row nor an explicit line, so the residue is a number that cannot grow in silence; what it does not do is fall. What preparation changed is the cost of the branch, not the choice: whoever rules may now read the exact passes the backwards reading buys, one row each, instead of an estimate.
owed.what_a_lane_may_do_and_has_done: Price the branch it may not choose. The backwards reading commits somebody to a number of fresh R-35 passes, and until 2026-08-14 that number was an estimate over a population nobody had turned into work: no commit range, no criteria locator and no brief existed for a single one of them. docs/receipts/verify-backlog.json, gated by tests/test_verify_backlog.py, is one prepared row per residue group -- the commits it spans by subject, the plan documents its stated completion criteria live in, and R-35's brief read from the runbook rather than copied, so a prepared pass cannot be handed a weakened one. This is a statement about the QUESTION a verifier would be asked and never about the answer, which is the same line the standing-dissent docket draws. It does not narrow the ruling: both branches remain exactly as written, and the row set is asserted equal to the ledger's own residue list so preparation cannot become redefinition.

answered.amendment: Amendment E — 2026-08-14, how a disposition transition is adjudicated
answered.the_ruling: A disposition transition is adjudicated BY CITATION, not by verdict, under three guards: the diff must be on a dispositions entry as the identity-keyed leaf_report classifies it; the cited ruling must be one a reader can open; and the leaf the entry describes may not move. The third guard is this amendment's own contribution -- citation can only ever excuse a change in what a payload SAYS ABOUT a number that did not change.

A quotation at its address is the opposite of a second home; a second home is a figure a reader cannot trace.

answered.amendment: Amendment J — 2026-08-15, how a campaign-authored justification string is adjudicated
answered.the_ruling: A campaign-authored justification string that asserts a fact about src-level vocabulary is adjudicated BY SOURCE ASSERTION -- a machine check binding the string to the predicate that produces it -- and never by an R-18 investigation, whose export excludes src/ by design. An oracle verdict on such a string is valid only for its export-verifiable portion, so a verdict that turns on a vocabulary its own limitations block declares out of bounds does not sustain a dissent; and the string MAY assert the src-vocabulary fact, because the machine check is what keeps it true. Three guards: one named producing site rather than a hand list, a check total over what the sentence quantifies over and in both directions, and nothing carved out but the src-vocabulary claim -- whatever such a string asserts about the cached corpus stays R-18's.

answered.amendment: Amendment Q — 2026-08-16, the lane a served walk-side need does not owe
answered.the_ruling: LANE-DECLARATION CORRECTION. A family whose walk-side need is satisfied THROUGH its declared serving lane does not need -- and must not declare -- a RECEIPT_WALK interpreter lane: one producer is precisely what the one-engine thesis demands, so a table that goes on asking a second lane for an answer the first lane already gives is asking for the thing criterion 8 forbids, and the deferral row underneath it is counting the absence of a defect. RECEIPT_WALK leaves _FAMILY_LANES for exactly the three measured families the defence resolver feeds, on the measured ground, in Amendment O, Ruling 1's shape -- WITH a machine check in BOTH directions and a reopening condition. Forwards: the named walk-side implementation reads the resolver's resolved state, source-asserted, derived per declaration rather than asserted per family, and a declaration nothing consumes fails the gate by name. Backwards: deleting the family's resolver interpreter flips its items to WITHHELD with a receipt naming the missing (family, defense_resolver) pair, never to a silent zero, run over every declaring owner on every check with an R-05 negative proving the red. Reopening: if a mechanic of one of these families ever authors walk-priced rows not fed by the resolver, the lane re-enters and the row reopens. This is not D-40's prohibition, because the declaration is corrected on a measured ground recorded in the umbrella with its check rather than edited to move a counter -- the walk consumes this family's numbers from the lane the family declares, and that is measured before the table moves and stays measured after it. Amendment K's three refusals stand as written: no interpreter is registered that emits fields nothing consumes, Amendment F's fourteen are not read as eleven, and what changes is a declaration that was wrong rather than a debt that was owed.

answered.amendment: Amendment R — 2026-08-16, the basic-attack swing terms, the census's reach, and a routed magnitude's owner
answered.the_ruling: FOUR RULINGS. (1) THE SWING TERMS. The from-declaration pricing stage gains the basic-attack swing composition, in the order the pair engine applies it: the packet is mitigated at ITS OWN resistance (Amendment N, Ruling 1), composed with the holder's static amps pre-mitigation (Amendment M, Ruling 1, already carried), then met by the target-side terms. Two of the three FOLD, because a pure factor on a linear mitigation composes into the declared magnitude and prices to the same real number -- the target's critical-strike damage multiplier and the plating multiplier. Warden's Mail's Rock Solid is NEVER folded: min(flat, per_hit * cap) is a capped flat SUBTRACTION and not a factor on a magnitude, it is applied to the crit branch and the non-crit branch separately BEFORE the deterministic blend, and it is carried as a term of its own -- the flat, its cap and its instance count transported on the declaration and subtracted per branch, floored at zero, before the branches are blended. The term rides ON the declaration, transported from the authored ledger rather than resolved again at the walk, for the reason Amendment N gave for the resistance; a declaration no basic-attack swing delivered carries none and prices exactly as today, so no retired family's number moves. Equivalence fixtures are seeded from the measured Caitlyn probe, BOTH inert and armed, on the reasoning that made Amendment M's fixtures cover amp != 1.0 and Amendment N's cover both windows. (2) THE CENSUS WIDENING. Amendment N, Ruling 2's census ranges over post-authoring packet mutation and the holder-amp folds beside it, and no census in that shape can reach a term applied while the packet is being AUTHORED; its prior green is recorded as TRUTHFUL under the old predicate, a fact about the census's reach rather than a defect in it. The predicate widens to range over AUTHORING-TIME mitigation terms as well -- every term _mitigate and _mitigate_basic_attack_swing apply, target-side as well as holder-side -- under the gate it already carries, with its R-05 negative updated so an injected authoring-time term turns it red, and no further family retires while the census shows an uncovered term. (3) ROUTING-FAMILY MAGNITUDE OWNERSHIP. secondary_target is a ROUTING family: it re-delivers SOURCE families' declared magnitudes at a second subject and declares no magnitude of its own (D-60, one producer per number). The copied packet is priced from the source family's declaration composed with the router's declared damage_share and attributed under D-62 at (source mechanic, secondary subject, event_id) -- the subject being what keeps that key clear of the same source mechanic's primary delivery -- with the routing recorded in provenance. The router's declaration carries exactly the routing facts it carries today, max_targets and damage_share, and gains no magnitude field. (4) COVERAGE. By integration act (R-12, R-32), the covering scenario set gains a scenario arming the enemy-held swing terms -- a defender holding Warden's Mail, with the plating multiplier and the crit-damage reduction in reach, met by an attacker whose delivery is a basic-attack swing -- and the coverage derivation READS the term mapping, the way repricing_window_declarations already reads the window mapping, so a further target-side swing term no scenario arms fails the capture on the commit that declares it. Armed means met: the mapping is a two-sided join, the defender's declaration on one side and a basic-attack delivery on the other.

answered.question: The tenth retirement attempt is the first whose family authors a packet DELIVERED AS A BASIC ATTACK SWING, and the from-declaration pricing stage cannot price one. Every family retired so far reaches the target through damage._mitigate and nothing else -- a resistance and the holder's magic amp, exactly what survival.pricing.price_declared_packet carries. Runaan's Wind's Fury bolt is priced by damage._mitigate_basic_attack_swing, which applies three further terms: the holder's basic amp, which the stage carries; the target's critical-strike damage multiplier, which is a pure factor and folds; and damage._apply_target_basic_damage_reduction's plating multiplier, which folds, beside a CAPPED FLAT SUBTRACTION which does not. min(flat, per_hit * cap) is not a factor on a magnitude, and in the deterministic reading it is applied to the crit branch and the non-crit branch separately before they are blended, so the cap bites on one and not the other. Measured on a Caitlyn holding Runaan's Hurricane and Blade of the Ruined King: the declaration prices to 76.54166666666666, which is exactly the pair engine's own figure while the three terms are inert, and the pair engine reads 63.60666666666666 once Warden's Mail's declared Rock Solid is armed on the defender -- 20.3 percent, on a term no committed coupled scenario arms.
